The query now authorizes via platform GodMode only, never throws to the client, and returns a validated org list (with a primary-org fallback if a full collect fails).

title: Pipeline file idle write storm stopped
summary: Deal autosave no longer retries patchDeal forever on conflicts or errors, which was burning Convex quota on open files.
body: Root cause: useDealWorkspaceEditor flush re-armed every 500ms after CONFLICT_DATA_CHANGED or thrown errors without adopting serverUpdatedAt or backing off.
Fix: adopt serverUpdatedAt on conflict, exponential backoff with a retry cap, skip no-op pending keys client-side, and skip unchanged deal patches server-side (no updatedAt/activity bump).
Write-storm console warnings ignore short measurement windows so a single early write no longer reports thousands/min.
Deployment: dpl_6cFpLc2jTsMUMsZBQdxZyvCTZUUo

title: Portal defaults: visual page builder
summary: Build portal templates on a live canvas with drag-and-drop, desktop/mobile preview, versions, and Set as default ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â without white-screening on open.
body: Settings ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ Portal defaults ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ Page builder is now a web-style builder: sticky top bar (Back, autosave, desktop/mobile, Preview, Versions, Save, Set as default), left section palette, and a center live canvas.
Drag sections from the palette onto the canvas or reorder existing cards; Preview mode shows a read-only page composition.
Hardened null config / empty version Select paths so opening or filling a portal default no longer crashes with ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…â€œCannot read properties of null (reading 'value').ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â
Still saves to portalDefaults / portalDefaultVersions ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â no second portal system.

title: Portal defaults form no longer crashes while typing
summary: Filling out portal default invite settings no longer white-screens with ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã…â€œCannot read properties of null (reading 'value').ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â
body: Root cause: name/description/checklist fields read e.currentTarget.value inside a setState updater. React clears currentTarget after the event handler, so concurrent/batched updates threw null.value.
Fix: capture the input string before setState in PortalDefaultsManager (list + create/edit form). Also hardened Settings pipeline stage style useState init.
Page builder version/welcome fields were already safe (eager reads).

title: Portal defaults builder: sidebar, header, and multi-column layout
summary: Build partner-style portals with a customizable sidebar, top header, and responsive multi-column section gridÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Ânot just a single-column stack.
body: Layout chrome: configure sidebar brand, nav items (label, icon, route), welcome/search/notifications toggles, and an optional floating action button.
Content grid: each section has a column span (3/4/6/8/12) so you can place stat cards, activity feeds, banners, and document widgets side-by-side like professional partner portals.
New section widgets: stat cards, notifications banner, search bar, activity feed, and pipeline cardsÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Ârole-filtered for client, lender, referrer, and deal partner.

Also includes the portal-defaults null.value typing crash fix (capture input values before setState).

title: Lender profile: Overview, Programs, Templates, Docs
summary: Lender profiles now use four tabsÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Âcontact & portal credentials, programs CRUD, lender task playbooks, and a fuller document vaultÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Âwithout duplicate template systems.
body: Overview: website, partner-portal URL with saved login credentials (org-scoped; encrypted at rest when CLIENT_PORTAL_FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set), linked contacts/reps, notes, deal parameters, and merge.
Programs: specialty summary plus structured programList create/edit/delete (same fields scenario matching already uses).

Docs: retitle, annotate, group, preview zoom, and full CRUD on lenderAttachments.
Enrich / Edit / Delete header actions stay on the profile chrome.

title: File header follows primary borrower
summary: The teal label next to the deal title now shows live primary borrower entity and individual names from Borrowers & GuarantorsÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Ânot the create-time client name.

title: Portal page builder: View as + real section setup

body: Settings ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ Portal page builder Preview is interactive: View as Client, Lender, Referrer, or Deal partner, then use sidebar, tabs, and cards to walk the experience (desktop/mobile width still toggles).

Contact cards use less padding, single-line notes instead of large empty textareas, compact role and borrower actions, and a clear Linked count / empty state.
Modals scroll inside the panel so the pipeline file workspace scroll owner is unchanged.

ExplorerÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢s + Tasks remains available; the command bar wraps on narrow screens so the extra action stays usable on mobile.

body: Open in window on Document Vault previously crashed with a missing DocumentVaultStateProvider error because the floating host sits above tab panels.
Vault navigation state now lives on the file workspace shell (one provider shared by the Documents tab and floating windows), so detach, browse, and return work without resetting into a second store.
Pipeline file scroll ownership is unchanged; floating panels remain overlays and do not introduce a competing page scroll.

body: On a pipeline file ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ Portals & Progress, every stacked block (Scenarios & Lender Match, Financial metrics, Action queue, Lender track, Internal workflow, Contact portal defaults, and client portal sections) shows a drag handle.

Order and visibility persist on the deal sheet via portalsProgressTabLayout, using the existing SortableSectionList pattern (no second reorder system). Layout gear menu can hide/show blocks or reset defaults.
Mobile keeps the Deal Info drag pattern (pointer distance activation) so vertical pans still scroll [data-pipeline-workspace-scroll].

body: Explorer toolbar now includes Download all (one ZIP of every downloadable file, preserving folder paths) and Download selected (ZIP of checked file rows). Download selected stays disabled until you check at least one file.
Each file row has a Download action next to View that uses the same signed storage URL path as preview. Compact Explorer rows also show selection checkboxes so multi-select download works on mobile.

title: Product Updates panel stays in front of the header

body: The Updates dropdown (and the Alerts inbox, which shares the same portal panel) now mounts into the appÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â€žÂ¢s global overlay root so transformed header chrome and overflow clipping cannot cover it.

Panel position is still fixed to the bell; only the stacking mount changed. Mobile scroll ownership is unchanged ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the list inside the panel scrolls locally with overscroll containment.

title: Product Updates stays above Contacts filters bar

Updates and Alerts now use the canonical CHROME_MENU overlay layer (above sticky list toolbars) and still portal to document.body with fixed positioning.
The Contacts sticky filter bar was also lowered to sit just above page content so it no longer competes with overlay menus. Scroll ownership is unchanged.

title: Internal Workflow: checkboxes, edit steps, templates

body: The Internal Workflow block on Portals & Progress was a read-only timeline with misaligned status dots. It is now a dense, clickable checklist that saves to dealData.workflow (same store as Deal Info).

Composer height, island padding, and spacing are tighter while Add file / Add link / Post note stay ~40px touch targets. Post note stays disabled until there is text, a link, or an attachment. body: Stronger borders and labels use DLC design tokens so section headers and field labels stand out more clearly against the form surface.
Money rows use a ledger-style layout so amounts line up consistently and are easier to scan while filling the statement.
Section 2 and Section 3 tables keep fixed column widths so labels, values, and related fields stay aligned across rows.
Installment debt Balance and Mo. pmt columns stay aligned for quicker comparison of outstanding balances and payments.
Calculation wiring is unchanged â€” this release is visual contrast and alignment only.

title: Document Vault: denser file & folder rows

body: File and folder rows in the Documents vault explorer use tighter vertical spacing in both compact and default density.
Selection checkboxes keep a ~40px touch hit area without stretching each row to 44px tall â€” so Download, Edit, View, and other actions stay usable.
Requirement cards, Unassigned chrome, and explorer toolbars are slightly denser. Scroll ownership is unchanged (page/workspace scroll, not a nested vault scroller).

title: File Details: TERM and shared fields save reliably
summary: Editing TERM (and other File Details fields) no longer fails with a Convex conflict when Generate Terms or other background writes update the file at the same time.
body: Root cause: pipeline.patch rejected the save with CONFLICT_DATA_CHANGED when expectedUpdatedAt was already stale from concurrent background writers (especially Generate Terms debounce).
Saves now retry once without the concurrency guard after a conflict, and Generate Terms background sync no longer takes that guard â€” reducing idle write storms on the file workspace.
Header RATE / TERM now prefer the shared File Details values (with Generate Terms as fallback) so the command-center metrics stay aligned with the block.

title: Deal Info Lenders: denser board & search
summary: The Deal Info Lenders block is tighter — less empty space around search and lender cards, with actions still easy to tap.
body: Board cards (Primary / Secondary / Considering) use less padding and put board role, Rejected, and remove on one compact action row instead of a tall empty side column.
Search helper copy is shorter, result rows are denser, and the Lenders block body padding matches denser Deal Info sections like Fees & Splits.
Primary controls keep ~40px touch targets on mobile. Pipeline file scroll ownership is unchanged — still [data-pipeline-workspace-scroll].

title: File header details panel no longer collapses
summary: Expanding the top-right file details chevron now shows Switch file, project assignment, and loan clients at full readable width on desktop and mobile.
body: Root cause: the header disclosure used a grid-rows collapse without an explicit full-width column track, so overflow-hidden + min-w-0 collapsed the panel to a one-word-wide strip.
The details panel now keeps full header width; Switch file sits in a dedicated column on large screens and stacks cleanly below on phones.
Project and file selects keep ~40px touch targets on mobile. Scroll ownership is unchanged — pipeline file still uses [data-pipeline-workspace-scroll].

title: File header shows project name left of stage
summary: The pipeline file workspace now shows the associated project name to the left of the stage pill — click it to open the project or switch to sibling files.
body: Project name sits in the top-left header cluster immediately left of the pipeline stage control.
Clicking the project opens a menu with Open project plus other files in that same project (current file marked). Files without a project show a muted No project label.

Sibling-file options reuse the existing pipeline switcher data filtered by project — same source as the header details Switch file list. Scroll ownership is unchanged ([data-pipeline-workspace-scroll]).

title: Portals & Progress: blocks start collapsed
summary: Opening Portals & Progress now shows every block collapsed so you can scan titles and expand only what you need.
body: Contact portal defaults, Action queue, Safe defaults, Link security, Client uploads inbox, Communications, and the other Portals & Progress sections all open collapsed on first visit.
Expand any block by tapping its header; drag-reorder and layout visibility still persist on the deal sheet via portalsProgressTabLayout.
Pipeline file scroll ownership is unchanged — still [data-pipeline-workspace-scroll].

title: Personal Financial Statement: fillable PDF export
summary: Download a client-ready fillable PFS PDF from the block header — right next to the Direct Link control.
body: A new download button sits immediately to the right of the Direct Link (chain) icon on the Personal Financial Statement block header.
It exports the full statement (applicant, assets, liabilities, Sections 1-8, and signatures) as a multi-page AcroForm PDF clients can type into and return.
Existing values are prefilled; blank schedule rows stay empty for the client. The shared Block PDF export helper can be reused by other blocks later.
Touch target stays ~40px; pipeline file scroll ownership is unchanged ([data-pipeline-workspace-scroll]).

title: Document Vault: move or copy to another project file
summary: When a loan file shares a project with others, folders, tasks, and documents can be moved or copied to a sibling file — structure preserved.
body: In Documents → Explorer, every folder, file task, and file row offers Move / copy to file… when the current file has at least one other loan file in the same project.
Pick the destination sibling, choose Move or Copy, and confirm. Folders keep nested structure; tasks bring their config and documents; document copies reuse existing storage (no re-upload).
The picker is a mobile-friendly OverlayShell bottom sheet. Actions stay hidden when there are no project siblings. Vault scroll ownership is unchanged.

title: Manage triage labels: modal fits the screen
summary: The Manage triage labels dialog no longer clips at the bottom — header and New label stay visible while the list scrolls inside the panel.
body: Opening Manage triage labels from a file Tasks block keeps the full panel within the viewport (max height ~90dvh), so the bottom edge and Close control stay reachable on short laptop and phone screens.
The label count and + New label controls stay pinned under the title; only the label list scrolls (overscroll-contained). Create/edit form content scrolls the same way when tall.
Rows are slightly denser while primary actions keep ~40px touch targets. Pipeline file scroll ownership is unchanged ([data-pipeline-workspace-scroll]).

title: Document Vault: download folders as ZIP
summary: Folder rows in the Documents explorer now have Download — packs the folder and all nested files into a ZIP with the original folder structure.
body: Unassigned folders (and every other explorer folder row) now show Download next to Link Contact / Trash, matching file-row actions.
The ZIP uses the existing vault download pipeline: every downloadable file under that folder is included recursively, with paths rooted at the folder name so nested organization stays intact.
Empty folders show a clear disabled state / toast. Larger folders show progress toasts so the UI stays responsive. Download all, Download selected, and per-file Download are unchanged.

title: Client portal PFS fields sync to the broker block
summary: Residence/business phone and the rest of the Personal Financial Statement from a client fill link or portal assignment now appear on the broker PFS block.
body: Submitting or autosaving a Personal Financial Statement from the client portal / direct fill link now merges the full structured statement into the file — including residence and business phone, city/state/ZIP, business name, assets, liabilities, and schedules.
Previously only a few summary totals were written into the deal, so phones and other header fields could look filled on the client side but stay blank for the broker.
If a client already submitted before this fix, ask them to Revise and Submit once more (or re-enter the missing phone and submit) so the broker block picks up the complete statement.

title: iPhone: top chrome clears the status bar
summary: On phones, the app header (menu, Updates, Sign out) now sits below the iOS status bar so controls are tappable.
body: Mobile master chrome now pads with the device safe-area inset at the top (same viewport-fit=cover contract already used for the home indicator).
Menu, help, refresh, Updates, alerts, and Sign out no longer sit under the clock / signal / battery on iPhone.
Pipeline locked-header height includes the inset so the single-row toolbar does not clip.

title: PFS fillable PDF: save to Document Vault
summary: The Personal Financial Statement PDF control now offers Download to computer or Save to Document Vault.
body: Clicking the fillable PDF icon on the Personal Financial Statement block opens a small menu (desktop) or bottom sheet (mobile) with two choices: Download to computer, or Save to Document Vault.

Save to Document Vault generates the same client-ready AcroForm PDF and creates a new vault document on the current loan file, placed in an existing PFS/Forms folder when present, or a new Forms folder.

Filename follows Personal-Financial-Statement-{file}.pdf. Loading and error toasts cover the upload; success reminds you to open the Documents tab. The shared block PDF export helper stays reusable for other blocks.
Touch targets stay ~40px; pipeline file scroll ownership is unchanged ([data-pipeline-workspace-scroll]).

title: Document Vault: Move on every file
summary: Individual files in the Documents explorer now show the same Move control as folders — move or copy any file to a sibling loan in the project.
body: Explorer file rows (inside tasks, folders, and Unassigned) now include Move next to Download, matching folder rows.
Works for any file type already linked to the loan — PDFs, images, and other vault documents. No content-type restriction.
Uses the existing Move / copy to file dialog (same project siblings). File tasks and folders keep their Move / copy actions.

title: Tasks block badge shows open count
summary: On Deal Info, the grey count next to TASKS now matches open tasks — not open plus completed.
body: The Tasks collapsible header pill previously counted every linked task, so a file with 1 open and 1 done showed “2” while the status pill correctly said “1 OPEN”.
The indicator now uses the same open-task count as the status badge and the “N open · M total” toolbar line.
Collapsed and expanded headers stay consistent; completed-only files no longer show a misleading total in the grey pill.

title: Tasks: grocery runs stay open when you check items
summary: Errands / groceries lists no longer collapse or flash busy after checking off an item — especially on phones.
body: Checking a grocery or errand item used to reset the row’s expand/collapse state whenever Convex refreshed the task. Large runs collapsed mid-shopping; small runs could jump or clear store collapse prefs.
Expand/collapse is now tied to the task identity (and type), not every field update. Errand and checklist toggles no longer lock the whole row, so checkboxes stay usable while saving.
Touch targets for check-off, expand chevrons, and store collapse are larger (~40px). Compact vs full list controls work both ways. Progress chips (done/total items) are clearer on the row.

title: Pipeline hub: stage pill works again; file details always visible
summary: Click a loan’s stage pill on the Pipeline list to change stage, and see client, project, and lender lines without hovering.
body: On Pipeline View (grouped list), clicking the stage pill on a row opens the stage chooser again and saves with the same update path as the file header.
A triage highlight badge on the row no longer sits on top of the pill and blocks clicks. Hidden row-action controls also stop intercepting clicks when they are invisible.
File identity lines — title with client, project, ★ lender, and ownership — stay visible at all times on hub rows instead of appearing only on hover.

title: Pipeline is now the default home screen
summary: Signing in or opening the app lands on Pipeline instead of Tasks. Brand and home links go to Pipeline too.
body: After sign-in, visiting / while signed in, or following the logo / monogram home control now opens Pipeline (/pipeline).
Signed-in visits to the login screen also bounce to Pipeline. Settings “Back to app,” not-found, and error recovery go to Pipeline as well.
Tasks remains available from navigation; it is no longer treated as the app’s first screen.

title: Open Document Vault files in a floating window
summary: View any vault document in a draggable window so it stays visible while you fill Deal Info, Financials, and other tabs.
body: On a loan file Documents tab, View (and opening a file) uses the same floating window system as pipeline blocks.
Keep a PDF, image, or other previewed file open while you switch tabs and copy details into forms — the window stays until you Return or close it.
Multiple documents can float at once. Preview still supports the same file types as the rich document viewer.

title: Document Vault: Move always available
summary: Move / copy to another loan file is always shown on documents, folders, and tasks — not only when project siblings already exist.
body: Previously Move was hidden when a loan had no other files in the same project, so solo files never showed the control.
Move now appears whenever you can edit the vault. If there is no destination yet, the dialog explains how to add or open another loan file.
Destinations include other files in the same project first, then other loans in your organization you can edit — same transfer path, broader targets.

title: Change link: tighter click target
summary: On borrower and guarantor cards, Change link and Remove link only respond to clicks on the label — not the empty space across the row.
body: Associated Contacts party cards (primary borrower, co-borrowers, guarantors) no longer stretch those controls to full card width.
The hit area matches the icon and text so accidental taps beside the label are less likely.

title: Float one Document Vault file without floating the whole vault
summary: Use Window on a file row or in the document preview to open just that document in a floating window.
body: In the Documents explorer, each file row now has View, Window, and Download. Window opens that document alone in a draggable floating panel — you do not need to float the entire Document Vault block first.

From the document View modal (and fullscreen enlarge), Window / Open in window does the same and closes the modal so you can keep working on Deal Info, Financials, or other tabs with the file beside you.
View stays a normal preview. Floating reuses the same rich document viewer (PDFs, images, and other previewable types).

title: Pipeline hub stage pill opens on first click
summary: Clicking a loan’s stage pill on Pipeline View opens the stage chooser immediately — the previous fix still left the picker blocked.
body: The earlier hub fix stopped overlays from stealing clicks, but the stage pill still swapped to a native control after click and never opened the chooser. Chromium requires showPicker during the same user gesture; calling it from a later effect fails silently.

Stage pills now use a transparent native select over the colored badge, so the first click opens the OS stage list. On Pipeline hub, contextual tips sit top-right (and ignore clicks outside the tip card) so they never cover stage pills.
File identity lines (title/client, project, ★ lender) stay fully opaque on hub rows. Ownership chips remain always visible when present.

title: Reset any team member’s password from Settings
summary: Workspace owners can pick a member in Team management, set a new password, and sign them out of all sessions in one step.
body: In Settings → Team management, use Reset password on a member row (or choose them in the Reset password form), enter the new password, then choose Reset password & invalidate sessions.
The member is signed out everywhere and must sign in with the password you set. Owner accounts are not reset from this form; only people with member-invite or role-management access can use it.
Passwords must meet the existing workspace policy (at least 6 characters). Deactivated members can still have their password reset so they can sign in again after reactivation.

title: Loan file Delete works reliably again
summary: Permanent delete no longer fails with a vague “Couldn't save” on hub bulk actions, and shared files with portal/vault data clean up safely.
body: Hub bulk Delete was sending the wrong argument name to Convex, which failed validation and showed only “Couldn't save — please try again.” Delete, Archive, and Restore now accept the correct identity and surface the real server message when something still goes wrong.

File delete cleanup no longer scans entire messaging/portal tables (which could time out on larger workspaces). Document Vault tasks, folders, notes, and related links for that file are removed with the loan file.
Owners still use Delete / Danger zone → Delete file. Shared recipients should use Leave share instead of Delete.

title: Leave a shared loan file (Google Docs style)
summary: If someone shared a loan file with you, you can Leave share — your access ends; the owner’s file stays.
body: On Pipeline hub, shared-view rows show Leave share (instead of Delete). Select only shared files and the bulk bar becomes Leave share.
Inside a shared file, Settings → Danger zone offers Leave share instead of permanent Delete.

Leaving removes only your explicit loan share. It does not delete the owner’s file or other collaborators’ access. If your access is inherited from a project or client share, you’ll see a clear message to change sharing there instead.

title: iPhone forms no longer auto-zoom on focus
summary: Focusing search, filters, and text fields on mobile stays at normal scale — and you can still pinch-zoom the page.
body: iOS Safari was zooming in whenever a form field used a font smaller than 16px (common on dense pipeline filters and search bars), and the page often stayed stuck zoomed in.
Every text input, select, and textarea on phones and touch devices is now floored at 16px so focus never triggers that zoom. Pinch-zoom remains available.
This replaces an earlier incomplete fix that Tailwind size classes could override.

title: iPhone Pipeline hub layout cleaned up
summary: Triage badges no longer cover titles, project lines wrap cleanly, the top chrome is less cramped, and the bottom nav no longer eats the last row.
body: On phones, triage badges (for example CLIENT: Action Needed) sit on their own row above the card content instead of floating over the loan title.

Client, project, and lender identity lines wrap instead of truncating mid-word. Stage, stars, and row actions sit on clearer stacked rows; the stray open/external-link icon is hidden on mobile because tapping the title already opens the file.

Masterpage header keeps search, updates, alerts, and account — help, refresh, live status, and theme controls move out of the narrow phone strip. Extra bottom spacer (with safe-area) keeps the last loan card clear of the bottom nav.

title: iPhone loan file: more room to work
summary: Opening a loan file on iPhone now keeps most of the screen for Deal Info blocks — funding/rate/owner sit behind Details, and the empty gap under the status bar is gone.
body: The file snap header was stacking safe-area padding twice and spreading title, stage, metrics, tabs, and favorites across too many rows, leaving only a sliver of workspace above the bottom nav.

Phone chrome is now two dense rows (deal name + stage/project) with Fibonacci-tight spacing. Funding, rate, term, and owner stay one tap away under Details (collapsed by default). Tabs and Favorites use shorter chips and less vertical padding.
Stage and project switchers stay visible without expanding Details. Safe-area under the Dynamic Island is applied once so controls are not covered and there is no large empty white band.

title: iPhone loan file: status bar and bottom spacing fixed
summary: Stage and title clear the Dynamic Island again, and the oversized empty band under the bottom nav is gone.
body: After the density update, the file sheet under-padded the top (status bar could cover the stage pill) and over-padded the bottom (stacked safe-area on the sheet body, scroll lead, and an 8rem spacer).

Top safe-area is applied once on the Vaul sheet (with a small breath so controls stay tappable). Bottom clearance is a single tighter spacer inside the file scroller so last blocks clear the nav without a dead white band under the bar.
Pipeline hub bottom spacing is unchanged.

title: iPhone bottom nav sits flush to the edge
summary: The mobile tab bar now paints edge-to-edge with only home-indicator inset — no more empty white band under the icons.
body: On iPhone, the bottom navigation looked floated: a large empty band sat under the icons above the home indicator because a frozen 24px / 1.5rem pad was stacked on top of safe-area padding.

The bar is now fixed to the physical bottom of the screen. Background and blur extend to the edge; icons sit above the home indicator using only env(safe-area-inset-bottom) inside the bar — no extra rem padding.
This applies everywhere the bottom nav shows (Pipeline hub, loan file, Tasks, Settings, and other routes).

title: iPhone bottom nav icons sit on the home indicator
summary: Tab icons no longer float above a thick empty band — they sit tight above the home indicator with only true safe-area clearance.
body: A prior fix removed stacked rem padding on the bar, but icons were still vertically centered inside tall min-height tap targets. That left empty chrome under the glyphs on top of the home-indicator inset.
Phone dock icons are now pinned to the bottom of their ~40px hit targets (empty height lives above). The bar still paints edge-to-edge; bottom padding is only env(safe-area-inset-bottom).
Applies everywhere the mobile bottom nav shows. Content spacers still clear the shorter dock.

title: iPhone bottom nav sits into the home indicator
summary: Tab icons sit lower — the large empty band under the dock is gone, with only a minimal inset above the home indicator.
body: Earlier flush fixes still reserved the full iPhone safe-area (~34px) under the icons, which read as a thick empty white band.

The bottom nav now uses a minimal home-indicator pad (about a quarter of the old inset, typically a few pixels) and pulls icons slightly into that zone while keeping ~40px tap targets. The bar paints as a continuous edge-to-edge surface with a thin top hairline — no floating shadow island.
Content spacers and batch bars match the shorter dock so lists are not over-cleared. Applies everywhere the mobile bottom nav shows.

title: Mobile side menu clears the status bar and covers the bottom dock
summary: Opening the hamburger menu on iPhone no longer leaves a white bottom strip or puts the brand under the clock.
body: The green SaaS navigation drawer now paints full-bleed from under the status bar through the physical bottom of the screen. Brand title and Funding & pipeline sit below the Dynamic Island via safe-area padding.
While the menu is open, the white bottom tab bar is fully covered and hidden so the More hamburger cannot show through a lower strip. Closing the menu restores the flush bottom dock.
Help center and related mobile panels also get matching top/bottom safe-area treatment for consistency.

title: No more white strip under the mobile menu
summary: Opening the green hamburger drawer on iPhone no longer leaves a full-width white bar above the home indicator — the menu and dimmer paint edge-to-edge.
body: A prior safe-area ship hid the bottom tab bar when the menu opened, but pipeline layout locks used CSS !important to force that white dock back on — so you still saw a full-width white strip under the green drawer.

Those locks now clear while the menu is open, the dock is hard-hidden with display:none, and the green drawer plus scrim stretch with true top/bottom inset (not a fixed 100dvh height that stopped short of the physical bottom).
With the menu closed, the bottom nav still paints flush to the edge so an orphan white band cannot peek underneath.
